meta.name: Collect and deduplicate local business leads from Google Maps with Figranium and Google Sheets

name: Collect local business leads from Google Maps for Free

parameters.content:
## Collect local business leads from Google Maps for Free

### How it works

This workflow collects local business leads from Google Maps based on a submitted form, compares them against existing records in Google Sheets, and only saves new leads. It first loads and caches current leads, fetches fresh results through the Google Maps lead source, splits the returned list into individual items, then routes each item through a deduplication check. Matching duplicates are ignored while unique leads are appended to the sheet.

### Setup steps

- Configure the form trigger with the fields needed for the lead search, such as business type, location, and any limits or filters.
- Connect the Google Sheets credentials and select the spreadsheet/range used to read existing leads in "Check Existing Leads".
- Configure the Figranium/Google Maps lead-fetching node with the required account/API access and map the form fields into its search parameters.
- Set the "Save New Lead" Google Sheets node to append rows to the correct lead database sheet, with columns mapped to the fetched lead fields.
- Verify the deduplication condition uses a stable unique value, such as business name plus address, phone number, website, or Google Maps place ID.

### Customization

Adjust the form fields, Google Maps search criteria, deduplication rules, and Google Sheets column mappings to match the type of local businesses and lead details you want to collect.

## Start and cache leads

Receives the search request from the form, reads the existing lead database from Google Sheets, and aggregates those records so later nodes can compare against them.

## Fetch and split results

Fetches local business leads from Google Maps through the lead source node, then splits the returned collection into individual lead items for processing.

## Deduplicate and save

Checks each fetched lead against the cached existing leads, appends unique records to Google Sheets, and sends duplicates to a no-operation endpoint.
